subject: psychology

moments.title: First split-brain patient
moments.body: Surgical sectioning of the corpus callosum to treat epilepsy yields patients in whom hemispheres can be tested independently.
moments.takeaway: Clinical surgery creates a natural experiment in lateralisation.

moments.title: Hemispheric specialisation studies
moments.body: Tachistoscope studies reveal each hemisphere has distinct capacities for language, spatial processing and emotion.
moments.takeaway: Lateralisation can be tested with controlled presentation.

moments.title: Nobel Prize
moments.body: Sperry shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology with Hubel and Wiesel.
moments.takeaway: Split-brain work was recognised at the highest level.

now.title: Beyond simple lateralisation
now.body: Popular 'left brain / right brain' narratives oversimplify findings. Network neuroscience emphasises distributed processing.
now.open_questions: How do consciousness and unified selfhood emerge from coordinated hemispheric processing?

reflection: Split-brain research is taught both for what it shows about the brain and for the philosophical questions it opens about selfhood.
